text:
mike: Hey team — customer acme-data noticed intermittent 429s during their nightly ETL starting ~00:10 UTC. They say burst credits should cover the spike but requests are getting `429: burst_credit_depleted` for ~20-40s then recover. Can someone help investigate?

alyssa: Pinged. Do we have the customer id + plan? Also can you paste a short log snippet and an example request?

mike: Customer: acme-data (acct: acct_9X7). Plan: growth. Log excerpt from their app:```
2026-03-16T00:10:12.123Z ERROR request failed status=429 body={"error":"Rate limit exceeded","reason":"burst_credit_depleted"} latency_ms=12
2026-03-16T00:10:35.456Z INFO retrying attempt=1
```Example of how they call our API (embedding backfill):
```bash
for i in {1..80}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme" -d '{"model":"embed-lite","input":["row"$i]}' & done
wait
```
They run that ~once per hour for a 15m backfill window.

raj: Thanks — most likely causes: many parallel small requests -> token bucket drains quickly; fractional refill rounding; or a policy that smooths over 60s but uses integer credits. Do we have their per-route token histogram? If not, can we repro with a synthetic concurrent run?

mike: I ran a quick repro from my laptop against a staging tenant with a similar config. Result: saw 429s starting at ~14s and lasting ~30s. Repro script I used:```python
import requests, threading
url = 'https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
def p(i):
  r = requests.post(url, json={"model":"embed-lite","input":[f"row{i}"]}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer test'})
  print(i, r.status_code)
threads = [threading.Thread(target=p, args=(i,)) for i in range(60)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```
Observed ~25% 429s at peak concurrency.

infra-bot: Metric snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/obs/tenants/acme-data/burst-credits?from=2026-03-16T00:05&to=2026-03-16T00:20 (shows credit bucket drained at 00:10:15 and refill beginning at 00:10:50) :chart_with_downwards_trend:

raj: That graph matches. Two actionable items: (1) short-term mitigation: enable client-side batching or add a small stagger/jitter to requests and backoff on 429s; (2) server-side: we can temporarily increase the tenant's burst window or apply a lenient smoothing policy for tonight's run while we root-cause. Also worth checking whether fractional credit accounting truncates sub-credit refills.

alyssa: I can apply a temporary policy change now if we want — need approval from product for policy changes. Also opening INC-5421 to track.

sophia: Approve temporary lenient smoothing for 2 hours. We should also notify the customer with clear guidance. Proposed customer message: "Sorry about the 429s during your ETL. We're applying a short-lived adjustment to your burst smoothing to let the job finish; as a next step, please batch requests if possible or add 50-200ms jitter between parallel calls. We're investigating a potential rounding issue in credit refill and will follow up in 24h."

mike: Sending that now. Also asked the customer to share exact start/end times + any client concurrency config.

raj: I'll instrument a test to check fractional credit accumulation at ms precision and run a deterministic load to reproduce rounding. If we confirm, fix will be small (use float credits and refill scheduler at 1s granularity).

alyssa: Temporary change applied: smoothing_policy="lenient" for acct_9X7 from 3167770020 to 3167773720 — noted in INC-5421. Monitoring.

mike: Customer acknowledged and says errors stopped after ~2 minutes. Thanks all. I'll keep the thread updated if they see more.

raj: Following up with a deeper RCA once we validate the fractional-credit theory. If confirmed, we should add an automated test in chaos-load to cover high-concurrency tiny payload patterns.

mike: Closing the customer-facing loop. Marking for postmortem in next week's eng-runtime retro. :thumbsup:
